question: Who is classified as a food handler in a food establishment?

options.A: Any person handling food or utensils directly
options.B: Customers consuming meals in the dining hall
options.C: Government health inspectors visiting the facility
options.D: Only the licensed manager of the kitchen

explanation: Food handlers include anyone who touches food, equipment, or surfaces during preparation and service. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h1)

question: Why is supervising food handlers critical in hospital or school settings?

options.A: It lowers the overall cost of buying food ingredients
options.B: Government policies ban cooking without direct supervision
options.C: Kitchen staff require constant entertainment while working
options.D: Vulnerable groups face severe risks from foodborne illnesses

explanation: Children and hospital patients have lower immunity, making infection prevention through supervision essential. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h1)

question: What is an example of a physical contaminant in food preparation?

options.A: Salmonella bacteria multiplying on raw beef
options.B: Pesticide spray absorbed by fresh tomatoes
options.C: Residual soap left on a rinsed plate
options.D: A strand of hair falling into the soup

explanation: Physical contaminants are foreign objects like hair, glass, or dirt that accidentally enter food. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h2)

question: How does cross-contamination typically happen in a busy kitchen?

options.A: Using the same cutting board for raw meat and salad
options.B: Washing cooking pots with cold water and local sponge
options.C: Cooking soup over an open wood fire for too long
options.D: Storing dry grains inside a tightly sealed plastic container

explanation: Cross-contamination occurs when pathogens transfer from raw items to ready-to-eat foods via unwashed tools. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h2)

question: What is the recommended minimum duration for proper handwashing among food handlers?
explanation: Thorough handwashing with soap and running water should last at least twenty seconds to remove transient microbes. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h3)

question: What immediate action should a supervisor take when a food handler has a deep cut on their finger?

options.A: Cover the cut with a waterproof, visible bandage
options.B: Send the worker home permanently without pay
options.C: Apply palm oil to the wound and continue cooking
options.D: Ask the worker to wear thick woolen gloves over the hand

explanation: Cuts must be covered with a secure, waterproof bandage to prevent bacteria from entering the food supply. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h3)

question: Which medical test is commonly used during routine screening of food handlers?

options.A: Stool microscopy for parasites and pathogens
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain

explanation: Stool checks help identify asymptomatic carriers of enteric pathogens like Salmonella and intestinal worms. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h4)

question: A kitchen worker reports to work vomiting and having watery diarrhea. What is the correct action?

options.A: Assign the worker to wash plates using hot water
options.B: Allow the worker to serve dry foods away from the stove
options.C: Exclude the worker from food handling duties immediately
options.D: Give the worker oral rehydration salts and direct them back to work

explanation: Workers with gastrointestinal symptoms must be removed from food handling to prevent widespread outbreaks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h4)

question: Which Nigerian agency is primarily known for national food and drug regulation and safety?
explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control regulates food safety standards nationally in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h5)

question: Why are daily internal inspections by kitchen supervisors important?

options.A: They replace the need for medical screening of staff
options.B: They prevent employees from taking unauthorized breaks
options.C: They reduce the quantity of ingredients used each day
options.D: They catch hygiene lapses before official government audits

explanation: Daily internal monitoring helps maintain continuous compliance and corrects safety risks early. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h5)

question: Why should food safety training for local handlers be conducted in simple local languages?

options.A: It ensures clear understanding and boosts practical compliance
options.B: Foreign languages are too difficult to translate into food terms
options.C: Government laws strictly prohibit English in commercial kitchens
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of printing recipe books

explanation: Using familiar language ensures all workers grasp safety concepts and apply them correctly during cooking. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h6)

question: How can a supervisor encourage kitchen staff to report equipment faults willingly?

options.A: By ignoring minor faults until an official inspector arrives
options.B: By creating a supportive culture that avoids unfair punishment
options.C: By forcing workers to repair broken stoves on their own time
options.D: By deducting money from salaries whenever a machine breaks

explanation: A blame-free reporting environment encourages staff to report hazards early before they cause contamination. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h6)
